source_review.notes: Reviewed the author-hosted Grossi-Vitter CSA paper, Ferragina-Manzini FM-index page, Makinen-Navarro survey, Grossi-Gupta-Vitter high-order paper, official SDSL repository and csa_wt implementation, and Navarro's author-maintained book page. All seven final chapter destinations returned HTTP 200. Complexity and compression statements remain qualified by the exact representation, operations, text model, sampling strategy, and computational model.

evidence: Checked T, n, SA, ISA, Psi, LF, BWT, C, half-open rank, suffix intervals, samples, locate, extract, self-index, and generation definitions.
Checked suffix ranks, normalized text positions, source offsets, and document-local coordinates are kept distinct.
Checked every modulo-n formula uses the declared unique-sentinel cyclic navigation model while pattern search uses terminated suffixes.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The chapter states rank interval conventions and sampling direction explicitly; plain parentheses used for inline variables do not change the mathematical definitions.

evidence: Independently sorted all suffixes of banana$ and reproduced SA [6,5,3,1,0,4,2] and ISA [4,3,6,2,5,1,0].
Independently recomputed Psi [4,0,5,6,3,1,2], LF [1,5,6,4,0,2,3], and BWT annb$aa.
Recomputed the ana interval [2,4), count two, source positions [1,3], and every sampled locate result.
Independently derived the aba$ exercise arrays, BWT ab$a, interval [1,3), and positions [0,2].
numerical_recomputation.notes: All array values and pattern positions use zero-based coordinates and half-open suffix intervals.

evidence: Substituted the definitions of Psi and LF through ISA and SA to derive both inverse identities.
Derived SA[i]=(SA[j]-d) mod n from Psi^d(i)=j and checked the LF direction separately.
Derived the half-open backward-search update from stable first/last-column correspondence and C plus rank.
Derived the at-most s-1 walk bound for samples selected by text-position residues and showed why rank-periodic samples lack that implication.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Compression bounds are attributed to cited representations and are not inferred from the bounded executable model.

evidence: Reviewed empty/absent patterns, repeated symbols, single-symbol texts, sentinel-reaching prefixes, unknown alphabet symbols, and long common prefixes.
Reviewed missing, repeated, or nonminimal sentinels; modulo wrap; inclusive/half-open rank mismatch; and sample-free Psi cycles.
Reviewed normalization drift, cross-document matches, large output cardinality, cancellation, corrupt lengths/offsets/padding, stale generations, and near-limit checked arithmetic.
Reviewed high-entropy, low-entropy, repetitive-version, small-input, construction-peak, and adversarial extraction workloads.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The fixture is finite and does not exercise collection ingestion, mapped persistence, corruption recovery, or scalability.

evidence: Verified SA and ISA are inverse permutations on all seven rows.
Verified Psi and LF are inverse permutations on all seven rows and BWT agrees with every preceding suffix character.
Verified repeated Psi navigation reconstructs the complete SA from the declared fixture samples.
Verified the model's interval and located occurrences equal independent suffix and direct-text oracles.
Verified exact eighteen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status with the repository safe snippet runner.
invariant_checking.notes: Fixture sample reachability is recorded as empirical evidence, not a general stride-bound invariant.

evidence: Reviewed the line-by-line permutation inverse argument against the unique-sentinel and SA/ISA assumptions.
Reviewed sample reconstruction against modular text advancement and the explicit premise that a compatible sample is reached.
Reviewed the sampling termination argument and its distinction between text-position residues and arbitrary suffix ranks.
Reviewed backward-search interval preservation against stable ordering of equal preceding symbols and half-open rank.
proof_review.notes: No proof is claimed for a concrete production encoding, high-order bound implementation, external-memory constructor, dynamic update algorithm, or recovery protocol.

evidence: Separated family-level CSA/FM-index concepts from one concrete SDSL implementation.
Separated permutation identities and sampling derivations from empirical compression and benchmark obligations.
The executable model explicitly disclaims compression, succinct support, scalable construction, general rank-sampling bounds, persistence, and production fitness.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter presents its proofs as scoped derivations and requires reviewed cited results for representation-specific asymptotic claims.

evidence: The Python standard-library model passed exact expected stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the safe verifier.
An independent Python recomputation reproduced every fixture array and inverse identity.
All seven chapter reference destinations returned HTTP 200 on the review date.
Local structure, link shape, ten examples, five exercises, five answers, and snippet checks passed before review completion.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production CSA/FM-index build, SDSL benchmark, entropy measurement, exhaustive text generator, collection index, mapped corruption campaign, concurrency test, or deployment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives SA/ISA/Psi/LF/BWT relationships, explains count/locate/extract distinctions, contrasts Psi- and BWT-centered families, and connects compression claims to explicit text and representation models.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed normalization and coordinate contracts, collection boundaries, sample tuning, output caps, construction peak, complete space accounting, immutable checked generations, atomic publication, corruption handling, recovery, and workload-specific benchmarks.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review establishes definitions and invariants; banana$ supports all core derivations; ten examples progress from permutations to operations and recovery; five exercises assess recomputation, proof, backward search, persistent design, and empirical selection.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/author/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Grossi, Vitter, Ferragina, Manzini, Makinen, Navarro, Gog, information-retrieval, bioinformatics, database, security, performance, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither a production CSA/FM-index implementation, concrete high-order compression bound, scalable constructor, dynamic concurrency, mapped recovery, universal compression, certification, nor deployment fitness.
